data.name: Bhargavi
data.gender_notes: Bhargavi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhargavi is the name of a celestial nymph in Hindu mythology. She is the daughter of sage Bhrigu and the wife of Lord Shiva. The name Bhargavi carries the meaning “Celestial Nymph” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhargavi usually hope their child will grow to embody celestial nymph and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bhargavi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Celestial Nymph.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhargavi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Bhargavi is a revered name in Hindu culture due to its association with the celestial nymph Bhargavi, who is believed to be the embodiment of knowledge, compassion, and grace. The name carries an aura of purity, wisdom, and divine blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Bhargavi represents the divine feminine energy, symbolizing knowledge, devotion, and the power of self-realization. She is a reminder of the deep connection between the individual soul and the ultimate reality. The name Bhargavi is believed to bestow grace and blessings on the bearer, inspiring them to seek knowledge, wisdom, and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhargavi signifies the radiant daughter of sage Bhargas, symbolizing wisdom and purity. Her name embodies the grace and strength of the goddess Saraswati, the deity of knowledge and learning.

vedic_reference.note: Not a direct Vedic reference, but derived from Sanskrit roots.

historical_references.reference: Bhargavi was an epithet of Goddess Saraswati, the Hindu deity of knowledge, music, art, wisdom, and learning. She is often depicted with a Veena, a musical instrument, and is associated with thecolor white.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, between 3rd Century BCE and 1st Century CE
historical_references.context: Bhargavi is a name associated with Goddess Saraswati, who was considered the patron goddess of scholars and students.

historical_references.reference: Bhargavi is also the name of the wife of sage Vyasa, who is traditionally believed to have authored the Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita. She is also known as Vyasaki or Vyasasri.
